text:
maria: quick heads-up, seeing steady memory growth on streaming sessions with tool-loop heavy workloads on dev-cluster-3. started ~12:20 UTC, consistent after ~45m of continuous chat/tool calls.
jon: can you paste the minimal repro or heap snapshot?
maria: reproducer: run long_chat_toolloop.sh (attached) against canary runtime. heap delta is ~350MB over 1h. here's trimmed pmap/sniped top output:
```
PID   VIRT   RES   SHR  %MEM  RSS_DELTA
12345 4.1G  1.2G  200M   3.1  +350MB over 1h
```
disha: any correlation with kv cache residency? iirc last week we changed page eviction heuristics in commit 7b3f2e.
maria: good point — I pulled kv stats from /metrics endpoint: active_pages/session went from 12 -> 48, pinned_pages/session 0.7 -> 20 over runtime. eviction_count stays low.
kai: that screams "anchored refs" — maybe toolloop holds tiny live refs to KV handles so GC can’t evict. can you grab a heap profile with symbols + kv page table snapshot?
maria: attaching lightweight capture (pprof heap) and kv dump snippet:
```
# kv page table sample
page_id,ref_count,state,owner_session
4096,3,active,session-873
4102,1,pinned,session-873
4110,2,active,session-901
...
```
jon: interesting: ref_counts increasing monotonically for a subset of pages tied to session-873. looks like reuse isn't kicking in — pages never go back to free pool.
disha: could be fragmentation + eviction threshold: if pages fragmented we can't coalesce and eviction candidate scan misses them due to policy (age+cost). did we change batching heuristics that affect prefix cache lifetime?
maria: batching change last deploy toggled "aggressive_continuous_batching=true" in runtime flags. it reduces kernel hops but may keep KV streams alive longer.
kai: if the batching keeps sessions open longer and toolloop holds iterators, we could be leaking page anchors. hypothesis: continuous batching holds a KV iterator ref until stream end, and tool loop adds callbacks that retain references across iterations.
jon: repro experiment idea: flip aggressive_continuous_batching=false and run for 2h. also set KV_EVICT_MAX_AGE=5m to force eviction. if mem delta stops, we have a strong signal.
maria: started flip on dev-cluster-3 at 3009991200, running now. will report at +30m.
infra-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-18T15:12 UTC — feature flags updated: aggressive_continuous_batching=false for canary group.
disha: also try targeted compaction: echo 1 > /proc/sys/kv/compaction_trigger (dev only) to force slab defrag. if fragmentation is root cause, compaction should reduce RSS.
maria: ran compaction at 3009991265, observed immediate 80MB drop, but growth resumed.
kai: compaction giving short-term relief suggests fragmentation + steady leak. not pure fragmentation.
jon: I pulled perf map during growth window. callgraph shows many callbacks in tool loop code path holding KVHandle::cursor() refs. likely code path that used to drop cursors per iteration now caches them across iterations for speed.
disha: risk/reward tradeoff: caching cursor saves kernel selection/batching overhead but can anchor KV pages. we should audit cursor lifetime and add weak references or explicit release at iteration boundary.
maria: prioritizing a quick patch: explicit cursor.reset() at end of tool-loop iteration. pushing branch: fix/toolloop-explicit-cursor-release -> will hotfix to canary if tests pass.
jon: also file a perf test to measure cost of releasing cursor each iteration (latency P95). if regression small, accept change. otherwise explore move to ephemeral handles with lease.
ops-bot: incident-note: tagged investigation-3009991234 in PagerDuty.
kai: next steps summary: 1) confirm mem stops when batching=false and eviction more aggressive 2) hotfix to release cursor 3) longer run with hotfix + continuous batching=true to validate no regression in latency 4) add metric for pinned_pages_per_session and alert when > 10 for 10m.
maria: update: after flip to batching=false, mem plateaued at +30m (no further growth). after flipping back and applying cursor-release patch in canary, run 45m -> stable. pushing PR for code review. :thumbsup:
jon: great. can we add unit test that ensures cursor.reset() happens on cancellation and loop exit?
disha: and add e2e regression test that runs long_chat_toolloop for 3h in CI infra-sim and checks RSS delta < 150MB.
maria: will add tests + monitor telemetry. thanks all for quick triage. :rocket:
